name: Simple Balance
tagline: Your personal ledger: ask about balances, spending and budgets, and stage transactions to review
description:
Simple Balance keeps one person's double-entry ledger. This is its hosted MCP server at `https://app.smpl.money/mcp` (Streamable HTTP), with up to 77 tools covering accounts and balances, transactions, categories and payees, budgets and forecasts, reports, CSV imports, staged transactions, recurring transactions and templates, and the activity log.

Sign-in is OAuth in your browser with dynamic client registration and PKCE, so there is no API key to paste. An **Allow this MCP client?** screen lists the scopes being requested: `ledger:read` reads, `ledger:stage` proposes transactions that change nothing until you commit them, and `ledger:write` changes the books. Tools outside the grant are left out of the tool list. Deleting your account, setting a password and billing are never reachable over MCP, and you can revoke the connection at any time under **Settings > Connected agents**.

Simple Balance doesn't connect to banks and can't move money. The server is open source (AGPL-3.0) at https://github.com/thtmnisamnstr/simple-balance and can be self-hosted.

Docs: https://smpl.money/docs/agents-and-mcp/

install.notes: After installing, connect your Simple Balance account. In VS Code or JetBrains, open MCP Servers, find simple-balance and press Authenticate. In the CLI, run `cline mcp` and choose Authorize OAuth. Sign in, then choose Allow access. Cline asks before each tool call unless you auto-approve it, so keep write tools out of autoApprove.
